facts.statement: Araripesuchus lived during the Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Araripesuchus is a genus of extinct crocodyliform that existed during the Cretaceous period of the late Mesozoic era some 125 to 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Araripesuchus is generally classified as a notosuchian within the clade Mesoeucrocodylia.
facts.quote: Araripesuchus is generally considered to be a notosuchian (belonging to the clade Mesoeucrocodylia), characterized by the varied teeth types and distinct skull elements.

facts.statement: The genus Araripesuchus was named in 1959 based on fossils from the Santana Group in Brazil.
facts.quote: The name of the genus was coined in 1959 with the description of the type species Araripesuchus gomesii, a notosuchian crocodylian from the famed Santana Group of the Araripe Basin in Brazil.

facts.statement: The species A. wegeneri was described in 1981 from Early Cretaceous deposits in Niger, Africa.
facts.quote: A second species, A. wegeneri was described in 1981. This species was discovered from Early Cretaceous deposits of Niger on the African continent, as opposed to the South American paleodistribution of the other species in the genus.

facts.statement: The species A. tsangatsangana was described in 2006 from Late Cretaceous deposits on the island of Madagascar.
facts.quote: A fifth species, Araripesuchus tsangatsangana was described in 2006. This species' type specimen was discovered from latest Late Cretaceous deposits from the African island of Madagascar.

facts.statement: The skull of A. buitreraensis measures 130 millimeters, making it the largest Araripesuchus skull known.
facts.quote: At 130 millimeters, the skull is the largest Araripesuchus specimen discovered to date.

facts.statement: A. wegeneri is estimated to have reached 81 cm in length, while A. rattoides could reach up to 1 meter.
facts.quote: A. wegeneri is estimated to reach 81 cm long while A. rattoides is estimated to reach up to 1 m.

facts.statement: Araripesuchus is distinguished by laterally bulged snout edges, most prominent near an enlarged maxillary tooth.
facts.quote: Araripesuchus can be distinguished by their laterally bulged edges of the snout, with the bulge being the most prominent around the area of an enlarged maxillary tooth.

facts.statement: A. rattoides possessed a highly enlarged, forward-pointing first dentary tooth called an incisiform, resembling rodent incisors.
facts.quote: A. rattoides also had the distinctive feature of a highly enlarged and forward-pointing first dentary tooth referred to as an incisiform, resembling the elongated incisors found in rodents (hence the specific epithet).

facts.statement: Araripesuchus had thin osteoderms covering its entire body, including multiple rows across the back and paired rows along the tail.
facts.quote: They also had thin osteoderms that covered the entire body, multiple rows of them across the back and paired dorsal ones along the tail.

facts.statement: Araripesuchus likely spent more time on land than in water, suggested by its non-keeled osteoderms, long limb bones, and upright posture.
facts.quote: The osteoderms were not strongly keeled, which, along with the long limb bones and shoulder, hip and ankle joints that suggest upright posture, indicate that Araripesuchus was probably more active on land than on water.

facts.statement: Studies show Araripesuchus grew slowly with annual growth interruptions, evidenced by lines of arrested growth in its bones.
facts.quote: Osteohistological study of a specimen of Araripesuchus cf. buitreraensis has found that it grew slowly over its lifetime, with it experiencing annual interruptions to its growth as evidenced by distinctly visible lines of arrested growth.

facts.statement: Fossils found in South America and Africa suggest a Gondwanan origin for Araripesuchus.
facts.quote: Araripesuchus remains have been recovered from the continents of South America and Africa suggesting a Gondwanan origin for the evolution of the genus.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses generally place Araripesuchus as a basal notosuchian.
facts.quote: In most recent analyses, however, Araripesuchus is placed as a basal notosuchian.

facts.statement: Some recent analyses question the validity of the genus Araripesuchus by placing A. wegeneri as a sister taxon to Anatosuchus.
facts.quote: However, recent phylogenetic analyses placed A. wegeneri as a sister taxon of Anatosuchus, questioning the monophyly of the genus.

facts.statement: The taxonomic classification of Araripesuchus within the suborder Notosuchia is sometimes marked as uncertain.
facts.quote: subordo: Notosuchia?

facts.statement: The genus Araripesuchus was first described in 1959 as A. gomesii from the Santana Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: El género fue descrito en 1959 como A. gomesii, un crocodilomorfo notosuquio de la famosa formación Santana, en Brasil.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen 423-R, consisting of a single skull articulated with part of a lower jaw, is housed in Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: El holotipo usado para describir el género, 423-R, está actualmente al cuidado de la División de Mineralogía y Geología en el Departamento Nacional de Producción Mineral en Río de Janeiro y consiste en un solo cráneo que se articula con la parte de una quijada más baja.

facts.statement: A second species, A. wegeneri, was described in 1981.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, A. wegeneri fue descrita en 1981.

facts.statement: The species A. wegeneri was discovered in Lower Cretaceous deposits in Niger, Africa.
facts.quote: Esta especie fue descubierta de depósitos del Cretácico Inferior de Níger, África

facts.statement: The species A. patagonicus was described in 2000 from a specimen found in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: El A. patagonicus fue descrito de un espécimen de la Patagonia argentina (MUC-PV 269) en 2000.

facts.statement: A skull measuring 130 millimeters is the largest Araripesuchus specimen discovered to date.
facts.quote: Con 130 milímetros, el cráneo es el espécimen más grande de Araripesuchus descubierto hasta la fecha.

facts.statement: A fifth species, A. tsangatsangana, was described in 2006 from Cretaceous deposits in Madagascar.
facts.quote: Una quinta especie, A.tsangatsangana fue descrita en 2006. Este espécimen tipo fue descubierto en los depósitos cretáceos de Madagascar.

facts.statement: The genus was originally assigned to the family Uruguaysuchidae by Price in 1959.
facts.quote: El género fue asignado originalmente por Price a la familia Uruguaysuchidae en la descripción original de 1959.

facts.statement: In 2000, Ortega et al. and other studies placed Araripesuchus outside of Notosuchia following the description of A. patagonicus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en el año 2000 cuando A. patagonicus fue descrito, Ortega et al. y varios otros estudios han situado a Araripesuchus por fuera de Notosuchia.

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis by Soto et al. united Araripesuchus with Uruguaysuchus, re-establishing the family Uruguaysuchidae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético de Soto et al. (2011) une a Araripesuchus con Uruguaysuchus, restableciendo la familia Uruguaysuchidae.

facts.statement: Araripesuchus lived from the Aptian to the Maastrichtian, between 121.4 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Maastrichtian (121.4 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils recovered from South America and Africa suggest a Gondwanan origin for the evolution of the genus.
facts.quote: Araripesuchus se ha recuperado de los continentes de Sudamérica y de África lo que sugiere un origen en Gondwana para la evolución del género.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses suggest Araripesuchus is more closely related to the Neosuchia clade, which includes modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: En algunos análisis filogenéticos, este es más cercanamente relacionado al clado Neosuchia, que incluye a los crocodilianos modernos.

facts.statement: However, many recent analyses place Araripesuchus as a basal notosuchian.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en muchos análisis recientes Araripesuchus es situado como un notosuquio basal.

facts.statement: There are currently seven recognized species within the genus Araripesuchus.
facts.quote: Hay actualmente siete especies reconocidas dentro del género Araripesuchus: A.gomesii, A.wegeneri, A.patagonicus, A.buitreraensis, A.tsangatsangana, A. rattoides y A. manzanensis.
